feature: New Window opens the front door
summary: New Window now opens a small front door instead of an empty editor: Open and a primary button in the title bar, the prompt bar, four starting templates and your recent captures. Picking a template names what the button makes and sets the mode, and the editor opens in its own window while the front door closes.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Press Shift Command N (or pick New Window from the Photonz menu bar icon).
Click the Design UI tile. The primary button in the title bar now reads New UI canvas.
Click New UI canvas (or press Return).
Check the chip beside the traffic lights reads Design, and that the front door has gone.
Open another New Window and double click Edit video: the New Video sheet comes up over it.
Open another New Window, point at a capture under Recent and use its Copy, Edit, Show in Finder or Delete buttons, or click it to open it.

evaluate: Does the front door feel like the place you would start from, or is it one window too many on the way to a canvas?
Is it clear that clicking a tile only picks it, and that the button in the title bar is what makes it?
Does the editor opening in its own window while the front door closes read as one smooth step?
Is the dimmed prompt bar fine to show before the agent can answer it, or would you rather it stayed hidden until then?
rough: The editor opens with the Design chip but the ordinary tool bar, not the mock's UI tool strip (Select, Frame, Component, Shape, Pen, Text, Measure, Hand): modes do not change the tool bar yet. Filed as design-mode-puts-the-ui-tool-strip-in-the-tool-b.

Two tile lines from the mock are over the 30 character chrome budget and moved into the tile's hover tip in the mock's words: 'Components, tokens, auto-layout' and 'Timeline, transitions, captions'. So Design UI and Edit video show a title with no second line (UX-PATTERNS §4).
The mock's header 'Start a project · pick a template' is over the budget, so the label reads Start a project and the full line moved behind it as its tip (UX-PATTERNS §4).
The mock's prompt placeholder, with its example, is over the budget: the field reads 'Describe what to create' and the mock's whole line moved into its tip (UX-PATTERNS §4).

The prompt bar is drawn but dimmed and takes no typing: the agent that would answer it is staged later in the plan, and the task asked for it to ship disabled (new-window-opens-a-front-door-with-a-starting-te notes).

The app goes further than the mock on the buttons the mock does not cover: Edit an image makes the button read Open Image…, Edit video reads New Video…, Capture & redline reads Capture, and a double click on a tile picks it and makes it in one go.

The primary button and Create are drawn white on the accent by hand, not with the system's prominent style, because in a window that is not key the system style drops its fill and left white text on the light window.
Recent shows capture history (the history strip's newest four), not every document you have opened; the hover action row is built from the history strip's own set and was not driven by a walk.
A guide's empty sample window (Your first capture) still shows the old card, because that guide points at its rows.
